questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of all vertebrates?
questions.solution: Vertebrates are defined as animals with a backbone, which is an internal skeletal structure. This means all vertebrates have an endoskeleton. Exoskeletons are found in invertebrates like arthropods. Feathers and hollow bones are specific to birds, not all vertebrates.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी सभी कशेरुकों की विशेषता है?
hi.solution: कशेरुक ऐसे जीव होते हैं जिनके पास एक कशेरुका होती है, जो एक आंतरिक कंकाल संरचना होती है। इसका अर्थ है कि सभी कशेरुकों के पास एक आंतरिक कंकाल होता है। बाह्य कंकाल कशेरुकों के बजाय अकशेरुकों जैसे आर्थ्रोपोड्स में पाया जाता है। पंख और खोखले हड्डियां पक्षियों के लिए विशिष्ट हैं, न कि सभी कशेरुकों के लिए।

questions.stem: What is the main reason given for classifying organisms?
choices: To make it easier to identify and study them
To reduce the number of organisms on Earth
To make them look more attractive
questions.solution: The main reason for classifying organisms is to make it easier to identify and study them. This allows scientists to organize and understand the vast diversity of life. The other options are incorrect because creating new species, reducing the number of organisms, or making them look more attractive are not related to the scientific purpose of classification.

hi.stem: संगठित करने का मुख्य कारण क्या है?

hi.solution: जीवों के वर्गीकरण का मुख्य कारण उन्हें पहचानने और अध्ययन करने में आसानी होती है। इससे वैज्ञानिक जीवन के विस्तृत विविधता को संगठित और समझा जा सकता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि नए प्रजातियां बनाना, जीवों की संख्या कम करना या उन्हें अधिक आकर्षक बनाना वर्गीकरण के वैज्ञानिक उद्देश्य से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of the five kingdom classification system?
choices: It includes only plants and animals
It is based on the habitat of organisms
It considers cell type, cell structure, and mode of nutrition
It separates organisms based on their size
questions.solution: The correct answer is that the five kingdom classification considers cell type, cell structure, and mode of nutrition. This is because the system categorizes organisms based on fundamental biological characteristics. The other options are incorrect because they rely on factors like habitat, size, or a limited range of organisms, which are not the primary criteria for this classification.

questions.stem: A student finds a small, cylindrical organism in a pond. What feature should they look for to classify it as an insect?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Body with jointed legs' because insects are characterized by having jointed legs. A cylindrical body is not unique to insects and can be found in other organisms like earthworms. Bilateral symmetry is common in many animals, and little segmentation is a feature of worms, not insects.

questions.stem: A scientist is trying to classify a single-celled organism with a well-defined nucleus and multiple cilia. Which group is it most likely to belong to?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Protozoa' because protozoa are single-celled organisms with a well-defined nucleus and often have cilia for movement. Bacteria lack a nucleus, fungi are usually multicellular, and algae are typically photosynthetic and not always motile with cilia.

questions.stem: A scientist discovers a new organism that has a true nucleus and can photosynthesize in the presence of light but behaves as a heterotroph in its absence. Which kingdom would this organism most likely be classified into?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Protista. Organisms in the Kingdom Protista are diverse and can include unicellular or multicellular eukaryotes that may exhibit characteristics of both plants and animals. This organism has a true nucleus, indicating it is eukaryotic, and can photosynthesize, which is a feature of plants, but it also behaves as a heterotroph in the absence of light, which is a characteristic of animals or fungi. This mix of traits is commonly seen in protists. The other options are incorrect because Animalia organisms are always heterotrophic, Fungi are always heterotrophic and lack chlorophyll, and Monera includes prokaryotes, which lack a true nucleus.

hi.stem: एक वैज्ञानिक नए जीव की खोज करता है जिसमें सच्चा केंद्रक होता है और प्रकाश की उपस्थिति में प्रकाश संश्लेषण कर सकता है लेकिन इसकी अनुपस्थिति में परपोषी के रूप में व्यवहार करता है। इस जीव को सबसे अधिक संभावना किस जगत में वर्गीकृत किया जाएगा?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर एककोशिका है। जगत एककोशिका में आये जीव विविध होते हैं और एककोशिक या बहुकोशिक यूकैरियोट्स हो सकते हैं जो पौधों और जानवरों दोनों के गुण प्रदर्शित कर सकते हैं। इस जीव में सच्चा केंद्रक होता है, जो इसे यूकैरियोटिक बनाता है, और यह प्रकाश संश्लेषण कर सकता है, जो पौधों का गुण है, लेकिन यह प्रकाश की अनुपस्थिति में परपोषी के रूप में व्यवहार करता है, जो जानवरों या कवक के गुण हैं। इस प्रकार के गुण सामान्य रूप से एककोशिका में देखे जाते हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि जंतुगण के जीव हमेशा परपोषी होते हैं, कवक हमेशा परपोषी होते हैं और क्लोरोफिल की कमी होती है, और बैक्टीरिया में प्रोकैरियोट्स शामिल होते हैं, जिनमें सच्चा केंद्रक नहीं होता है।

mr.stem: एका वैज्ञानिकाने नवीन जीव शोधला ज्याचे खरे न्यूक्लियस आहे आणि प्रकाशाच्या उपस्थितीत प्रकाशसंश्लेषण करू शकतो परंतु त्याच्या अनुपस्थितीत परपोषणक असतो. हा जीव जास्तीत जास्त कोणत्या जगतात वर्गीकृत केला जाईल?

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms would be classified in the Kingdom Monera?
choices: A multicellular organism with a cell wall and chlorophyll
A unicellular organism with a true nucleus
A unicellular organism without a nucleus
A multicellular organism with a contractile vacuole
questions.solution: The correct answer is a unicellular organism without a nucleus. Kingdom Monera includes prokaryotes, which are unicellular organisms that lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. The other options are incorrect because organisms with a true nucleus belong to the Kingdom Protista or other eukaryotic kingdoms, and organisms with a cell wall and chlorophyll are typically plants, while those with a contractile vacuole are often protists or other eukaryotes.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of classification in biology?
choices: To make it easier to identify and study organisms
To group organisms based on unrelated features
To change the names of organisms
questions.solution: Classification in biology organizes living things in a way that simplifies their identification and study.
